turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics

**What the training data says works best (>19 %):**
- **Absorbers:** mixed-cation, mixed-halide Pb perovskites (FAMAPbBrI, CsFAMAPbBrI, FAMAPbI) — good defect tolerance, tunable ~1.55–1.6 eV gap, good film quality from spin-coating. Sn-containing, Bi, Sb, wide-gap Br-only compositions all sit far lower.
- **n-i-p:** SnO₂ (c or np) or TiO₂-c/mp ETLs with Spiro-MeOTAD (or engineered HTLs like **DM**, used in the 22.9 % record with OAI passivation) and Au back contact. Interface passivation layers (CH₃O-PEIA, 2D capping, QD interlayers) push devices to 20–22 %.
- **p-i-n:** C60/PCBM + BCP with **PTAA** (or SAM 2PACz) and Cu/Ag contacts reach 18–20.3 % (e.g., C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu on FTO = 20.1; PCBM|C60|BCP / PTAA / Ag = 20.3). PEDOT:PSS caps devices lower (~13–16) due to its poor selectivity/work-function mismatch.

**Scanning the pool:**

- **c019** — FAMAPbBrI, n-i-p, TiO₂-c|mp, **DM** HTL, Au: essentially the record-holding stack (22.91 % used OAI|DM on the same ETL/absorber). DM has deep HOMO, excellent hole selectivity and less parasitic doping than Spiro. Top pick.
- **c093** — CsFAMAPbBrI, p-i-n, FTO, PCBM|BCP, **PTAA**, Ag: direct analog of the 20.1–20.3 % PTAA-based inverted devices; PTAA gives low interface recombination and good VOC.
- **c085** — CsFAMAPbBrI, p-i-n, C60|BCP, **PTAA|PFN-Br**, Cu: same family as the 18.35–20.1 % PTAA/Cu devices; PFN-Br wetting/dipole layer improves the buried interface — expect ~19–20 %.
- **c062** — FAMAPbBrI, n-i-p, SnO₂-np|PCBM, Spiro, MoO₃|Au: SnO₂/fullerene bilayer passivates the buried interface (analogs at 19–20.5 %), MoO₃ buffer protects the contact.
- **c092** — FAMAPbI, n-i-p, SnO₂-np, Spiro, MoO₃|Ag: mirrors the 19.5–20.2 % SnO₂-np/Spiro devices (FAPbI on SnO₂-np/Spiro/Au = 20.2; MoO₃|Ag analog = 19.6).

Close runners-up (c034, c038, c047, c008, c079) are solid ~18–19 % recipes but lack the extra interface engineering or the proven top-tier HTL.

**Final: c019, c093, c085, c062, c092**
